task: Write comprehensive tests for stopwatch widget API
summary: Created 50 tests covering the stopwatch API endpoints: CRUD operations, start/stop/reset/lap functionality, multiple stopwatch independence, edge cases, persistence, and security.

edge_cases_documented.title: Unicode labels
edge_cases_documented.description: Labels can contain emoji and non-ASCII characters

edge_cases_documented.title: XSS attempts in labels
edge_cases_documented.description: HTML/script tags are stored as-is (not executed)

edge_cases_documented.title: Non-existent stopwatch operations
edge_cases_documented.description: All operations on non-existent IDs return success: false

edge_cases_documented.title: Label boundary - max length
edge_cases_documented.description: Labels at exactly 100 chars accepted, 101+ rejected

edge_cases_documented.title: Idempotent start/stop
edge_cases_documented.description: Starting running or stopping stopped stopwatch doesn't error

edge_cases_documented.title: Reset while running
edge_cases_documented.description: Reset stops and clears elapsed time in one operation

edge_cases_documented.title: Empty/null labels
edge_cases_documented.description: Both empty string and null labels result in empty string

edge_cases_documented.title: Elapsed time accumulation
edge_cases_documented.description: Multiple start/stop cycles accumulate elapsed_ms correctly

handoff_notes.to_frontend_dev: API tests pass. Frontend can implement UI for spawning and controlling multiple stopwatches. Each stopwatch updates independently.
handoff_notes.to_backend_dev: Backend implementation is complete and passing all tests. No changes needed.
handoff_notes.timing_note: Tests use time.sleep(0.01-0.02s) for timing verification. If flaky, mock datetime module instead.
